coverage.note: Built from headlines and RSS descriptions published between 08:00 on Saturday and 08:00 on Tuesday Copenhagen time, from 132 feeds at seventeen publishers, all polled successfully. Danish outlets decide what is news; international titles are linked where they cover the same story. Nothing else was read.

copy.headline: Government plans dearer electric cars and SU cut for 81,000 students

extended.text: The government plans to raise the registration tax on electric cars from 1 January 2027 and to stop the SU student grant for 81,000 students who live at home and whose parents together earn more than 710,000 kroner a year. Four ministers told Berlingske on Monday that the money will help pay for free dental care, lower taxes and a transition in farming in a finance bill still to be presented.

The tax-free threshold for electric cars falls from 419,300 to 366,200 kroner, TV 2 reports. The government also wants a cap on interest deductions and tougher work requirements for graduate unemployment benefit.
The motorists' organisation FDM estimates that the tax on a Tesla Model Y Long Range could rise by almost 28,000 kroner, and on a VW ID.4 Style by about 10,300 kroner.

Thomas Møller Sørensen, head of the car industry at Dansk Industri, calls the rise an 'own goal' while an expert group on car taxation has yet to report. Upper-secondary students call the SU proposal 'an attack on young people', DR reports.

copy.headline: EU ministers hold back on von der Leyen's hybrid-attack protocol

standard.text: EU defence ministers on Monday held their first discussion of an emergency security protocol proposed by Ursula von der Leyen, the Commission president. Under the protocol, all member states would convene when one triggers it. Altinget describes a lukewarm reception.

Politiken reports that some countries want the procedure so the EU can respond faster to Russian attacks, while others hesitate and point to Nato. Kaja Kallas, the EU's foreign policy chief, said there must be no overlap with Nato's tasks.
Kallas also said Europe must arm faster to meet its 2030 goal of defending itself. She said no country offered Patriot missiles for Ukraine or the ships the Aspides mission needs.

copy.headline_short: EU ministers hesitate on hybrid protocol
copy.deck: Some capitals want a faster European answer to Russian sabotage, while others fear treading on Nato's ground.

copy.headline: Importer beats Novo to Danish launch of Wegovy pill

standard.text: Parallel importer 2care4 on Monday began sending Novo's Wegovy weight-loss pill onto the Danish market ahead of Novo's own launch, 2care4 told MedWatch.

2care4 buys the pill in Germany and repackages it for Danish pharmacies. A pack will cost between 2,838 and 3,876 kroner depending on dose, according to 2care4. TV 2 reports that Danes will not be able to buy it for several days.

Mads W. Ø. Larsen, country manager at Novo Denmark, said Novo was not surprised but could not say when it would launch the pill in Denmark or at what price. Novo has launched it in the US, the United Arab Emirates, Britain and Germany.

copy.headline_short: Importer beats Novo to Wegovy pill
copy.deck: A parallel importer is bringing the weight-loss pill in from Germany at up to 3,876 kroner a pack, and Novo cannot yet say when its own launch will come.

callouts.text: The market for weight-loss medicine is developing extremely fast, and demand is enormous. With this launch we are showing the value of parallel import.

copy.headline: Magdalena Andersson gives up forming Sweden's government

standard.text: Magdalena Andersson, the Social Democrats' leader, gave up trying to form a government on Monday, after Vänsterpartiet backed the Moderates' Andreas Norlén, who was re-elected speaker of the Riksdag the same day.
The speaker names who tries next, and Norlén opens new talks on Wednesday.

Vänsterpartiet announced its support on Sunday evening, ignoring pressure from the Social Democrats, whose group leader, Lena Hallengren, called it 'a betrayal of all the voters who voted for change'.
Alfred Arnborg, an analyst at Tænketanken Europa, tells Kristeligt Dagblad that the Moderates will get a chance and also fail, before the Social Democrats try again.

copy.deck: A left-wing vote for a Moderate speaker hands Andreas Norlén the choice of who tries next.

lede.text: Magdalena Andersson has abandoned her attempt to form a Swedish government after Vänsterpartiet backed the Moderates' Andreas Norlén, re-elected speaker on Monday.

copy.headline: Police bail RAF Fairford suspects as Trump says he would have held them

standard.text: The five men arrested near RAF Fairford on Sunday, all British citizens, were released on police bail on Monday. Laurence Taylor, head of British counter-terrorism policing, said they face strict conditions on their movements and contacts.

The US military has used the base since March for strikes on Iran. Donald Trump said he would not have released the men and, asked about an Iranian link, answered 'possibly'. Marco Rubio, the US secretary of state, said a foreign actor was 'clearly involved'. Iran calls the accusations 'baseless'.
Information, noting that no explosives were found, reads the episode as psychological warfare or a bad spy novel.

copy.deck: Washington hints at Iran, Tehran calls the claims baseless, and the five British men remain under investigation.

callouts.text: To be absolutely clear, that does not mean the investigation is over.
